headline: Models expose emergent coexistence and coevolutionary structure in ecological systems
label: Modeling Ecological Coexistence And Coevolution
summary: Recent March 2026 models separate model-generated interaction structure from biological structure across ecosystems and pathogen evolution.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit mathematical modeling used to ask which structure is intrinsic to a system and which is generated by the modeling framework. The plankton preprint shows that interlayer diffusion synchronizes Turing patterns and enhances noise robustness, with zooplankton more sensitive. A unified differential-equation model of coexistence mechanisms reports bimodal diversity patterns as habitat fragmentation increases. A pathogen preprint argues that infection spread and antigenic strain evolution, usually modeled separately, should be coupled through host immune feedbacks. The published study shows that pairwise-interaction ecological models generate emergent coexistence through indirect effects, limiting reductionist explanations. What is distinctive is the treatment of emergent, model-dependent interaction structure as a result to be tested across ecological and coevolutionary scales.
